body:
Source: GitHub issue #774 (release-audit class false-green, P1-high). Re-verified on main @ bf3d546a: `packages/spec-lint/lib/classify.mjs` (`applyLlmDemotion`, around line 158) builds `new Set(llmResult.vacuous ?? [])` and tests membership with the numeric loop index `subIdx` from `verifiedIndices.entries()`. If the model answers with string indices (`{"vacuous": ["0","1"]}` — a perfectly plausible JSON encoding the prompt does not forbid), `Set.has(0)` is false for every entry, zero criteria are demoted, and `spec-lint --llm` prints `all criteria verified` and exits 0 having checked nothing — with no warning anywhere. The same fail-open exists one layer up in `packages/spec-lint/lib/llm.mjs:53`: `vacuous: Array.isArray(parsed?.vacuous) ? parsed.vacuous : []` silently turns a missing/misshaped `vacuous` field (a bare array of indices, or an object with a differently-named key) into `[]` — "nothing vacuous" — instead of "could not check".

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER. Package `packages/spec-lint`: bin/spec-lint.mjs (parses `--llm`, wires the LLM call, exits 0 pass / 1 operational error / 2 gate fail), lib/llm.mjs (`callLlmDemotion`-style function around line 48-56 that calls `complete()`/`extractJson()` and returns `{vacuous, reason}`), lib/classify.mjs (`applyLlmDemotion(classified, llmResult, verifiedIndices)` — the demotion loop). Tests: `npm test -w packages/spec-lint`.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. In lib/llm.mjs, after `extractJson`, validate the parsed payload rather than coercing failure into `[]`: the payload must have a `vacuous` field that is an array; every element, after `Number(v)`, must be an integer in `[0, verifiedCount)` (pass the count of criteria sent to the LLM in). If the field is missing, not an array, or ANY element fails that check, throw an Error whose message identifies the problem (missing field vs. wrong type vs. out-of-range index vs. non-integer) — this propagates to the caller's existing `opError` path (exit 1, "could not check"), never a silent `[]`.
2. On success, return `vacuous` as the NUMERIC indices (post-`Number()` coercion), so `classify.mjs`'s `Set.has(subIdx)` comparison works whether the model answered with numbers or numeric strings — this is the one-line normalization that recovers the common deviation, matching how coldstart's #594 fix accepted a bare array as the common deviation rather than rejecting it outright.
3. `applyLlmDemotion` in classify.mjs no longer needs its own `?? []` fallback once llm.mjs's contract is enforced — but keep a defensive `Array.isArray` assertion there too (belt-and-suspenders; a wrong-shaped payload reaching classify.mjs from ANY caller, present or future, must still fail loudly rather than iterate over `undefined`).
4. No warning-then-continue: an unusable vote payload is always an operational error (exit 1), never a silent pass.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 `{"vacuous": ["0","1"], "reason":{...}}` (string indices) is accepted and demotes the SAME criteria as `{"vacuous": [0,1], ...}` would. verify: `node --test packages/spec-lint/test/llm-vote-coercion.test.mjs`
- AC2 `{"result":"ok"}` (missing `vacuous`), `{"vacuous": null}`, `{"vacuous": "none"}`, `{"vacuous": [0, "abc"]}` (one non-numeric entry), and `{"vacuous": [0, 99]}` (index out of range for a 3-entry verified set) each throw / propagate to exit 1 with a message naming the specific problem — none demote anything and none exit 0. verify: `node --test packages/spec-lint/test/llm-vote-coercion.test.mjs`
- AC3 A bare top-level array response `[0,1]` (no `vacuous` wrapper) is treated the same as AC2 (still an operational error — this package's fix, unlike coldstart's #594, does NOT special-case a bare array, because the prompt asks for an object; state this explicitly in a test as a deliberate design decision, not an oversight). verify: `node --test packages/spec-lint/test/llm-vote-coercion.test.mjs`
- AC4 CLI integration: with `ADLC_GATE_MOCK_RESPONSE` (or whatever mock seam this package already has — check bin/spec-lint.mjs and existing tests for the pattern) set to a string-index payload, `spec-lint --llm` demotes and exits 2 (there were vacuous criteria); set to a malformed payload, it exits 1 with a clear stderr message, never `all criteria verified`. verify: `node --test packages/spec-lint/test/llm-vote-coercion.test.mjs`
- AC5 Existing suite green (39/39 baseline — confirm the actual count; if a test pinned the silent-[] fallback, rewrite it and say so in the PR body). verify: `npm test -w packages/spec-lint`
- AC6 Mutation gate green on the branch. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0 (also run `--max 80` once locally before review)

OUT OF SCOPE: issue #433 (which verification methods get credited) — this ticket is about vote coercion/validation only, not the demotion policy itself.

PROCESS (ADLC). Work only in your assigned worktree. P3: the rails on this ticket are frozen — if the fix appears to require editing a rail path, STOP and report; never set ADLC_RAILS_BYPASS. P4: TDD — write test/llm-vote-coercion.test.mjs first, run it RED, then implement. P5 before opening the PR: `npm test -w packages/spec-lint`, `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` (exit 0), then the cross-model review loop (see lane instructions) until a round is clean. Do not add gate-manifest entries. Keep the diff to packages/spec-lint/** and this ticket's shard. PR title `fix(spec-lint): ...`, body must contain `Closes #774`.
title: spec-lint: coerce and validate --llm vacuous-vote indices; fail closed (exit 1) on an unusable payload instead of silently demoting nothing
